Subject: Important information: Corvane children’s ibuprofen dosing-syringe recall

We know many families are worried and angry, and we want to explain clearly what happened and what parents should do now.

Which products are involved?

The recall covers Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry flavour), 120 mL bottles, lots CV6114A and CV6114B, with expiry 08/2027. Please check the lot number on the bottom of the box first. Other lots are not part of this recall. If you cannot find or read the lot number, bring the box and bottle to us.

The ibuprofen liquid itself meets all product specifications. It is not contaminated, and the medicine is not the problem. The recall is because of a printing error on the dosing syringe supplied inside these boxes.

The syringe markings are labelled at half their actual volume. For example:
- The mark labelled 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL.
- The mark labelled 5 mL actually measures 10 mL.

A caregiver following those markings could therefore give approximately twice the intended dose.

What should you do with the product?

If your box has lot CV6114A or CV6114B, stop using and discard the supplied syringe. Do not try to calculate or compensate for the incorrect markings yourself.

Correctly marked replacement oral syringes are expected from Northshore before noon today, Monday, November 9. They will be free, with no receipt required. Bring the product and box if you can, and we can also check the dosing instructions with you. You may instead return the affected product for a full refund. We will also be open this Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. for exchanges.

What if your child may have received too much?

If your child was given a dose using one of these syringes, or you have any doubt about how much was given, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017. They are available 24 hours a day. Do not wait for symptoms to appear.

They can assess your child individually. The right advice depends on factors such as your child’s weight, the amount and number of doses given, symptoms, and medical history, including kidney problems. There is no single answer that is safe to give every family online. Do not give another dose until the poison centre or a doctor tells you it is okay.

Call 911 or go to the emergency department immediately if your child is extremely sleepy or difficult to wake, vomits blood, has a seizure, or is not urinating.

We received the recall notice on the evening of November 6. On the morning of November 7, we removed the remaining affected bottles from the shelf and posted notices on the front door and in the children’s medicine aisle. Because these were over-the-counter purchases, we do not have customer profiles or phone numbers for most purchasers, so we were not able to identify and telephone everyone who bought a bottle.

We understand how frightening that is for parents, and we are sorry for the fear and confusion this situation has caused. Please contact us or come in so we can help you check your product and decide on the next step.

Rania and the Cedarbrook Pharmacy team
